k7f671035: For The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, temples are the most sacred buildings on earth. They are not chapels where Sunday services are held — they are special places dedicated to sacred ordinances that bind families together not only in this life, but also for eternity.
k17c08f22: In the scriptures, temples have always been the place where God meets with His children. From the tabernacle of Moses to the temple of Solomon, the temple represents the presence of God on earth.
k8518578a: Sacred ordinances are performed in temples that cannot be performed anywhere else. These ordinances include:
kad0f0098: <t1>Baptism for the dead</t1> — we can perform this ordinance on behalf of our ancestors who died without the opportunity to receive it
k184f610a: <t1>The endowment</t1> — an ordinance in which members make sacred covenants with God and receive spiritual instruction
k4356e31c: <t1>Sealing</t1> — eternal marriage and the uniting of families forever, not just “until death do you part”
k09446e66: We believe the family can be eternal. The love we feel for our loved ones does not have to end with death. In the temple, a family can be “sealed” by the power of the priesthood — what is bound on earth is bound in heaven.
k285e6a77: This doctrine gives a completely different perspective on loss, grief and family relationships. It is not just about living together during this life — it is about being together forever.
k1eb9af82: Temples are open to the public only when they are newly built or renovated, during an “open house” period. Afterward, only Church members who live its principles may enter. However, the temple grounds are always open and many have visitors' centers where anyone can learn more.
keed07d28: If you are curious about temples or want to learn more about the ordinances performed in them, we would be happy to explain.
kb0e70d91: Talk to us and we will explain everything about temples, their ordinances and why they are so meaningful to us.
